title: Plasticity injection at handoff: 88 fresh zero-output GELU units per trunk MLP (d_ff 1280 -> 1368 for RL only), filling the 10M cap, on the 153-claude width-384 Lean incumbent (9,963,792 params)
description: P24 x P19/P22 handoff plasticity (not P01/P02): pretraining is byte-identical to 153-claude, and at handoff every trunk MLP gains 88 units with random fc1 rows and zero fc2 columns, so the handed-off function and round-1 sampler are unchanged while RL's AdamW gets 406,032 fresh parameters (the rest of the 10M cap). Plasticity injection (Nikishin et al. 2023) for expert iteration: 129, 025 and 131 say less-annealed, less-averaged handoffs fine-tune better, and fresh units add uncommitted capacity for 7+ line proofs without disturbing anything pretraining learned.
hypothesis: Expert iteration (4 rounds x 600 AdamW steps at 3e-4) has to teach proofs longer than any pretraining record, starting from a model whose every parameter is committed to <=6-line next-token prediction. The Lean record says handoff plasticity is a lever: raising the LR floor to 0.3 (129) won although round 1 got worse, because RL climbed faster (+478 vs +384 r1->r4), while weight averaging (025 EMA -66, 131 SWA -10) improved greedy and round 1 but slowed the climb. Plasticity injection (Nikishin et al. 2023) adds capacity that is plastic by construction and cannot disturb the pretrained function: zero fc2 columns make the new units silent at handoff, so round 1 samples exactly the incumbent's function, and Adam's per-parameter normalization moves those columns by ~lr per step from the first RL step, so the 88 units per block become new features learned only from RL's longer proofs. The width series (151, 153) also says unused cap is worth spending. Prediction mechanism: same pretraining and round-1 numbers as 153 within its lottery, a steeper r1->r4 RL climb, and more eval solves at L 7-9. Failure modes: (a) the fresh units' early Adam updates on near-zero-signal columns are random writes that make rounds 2-4 sample worse; (b) 4% more parameters is too small to move a 3-seed mean whose sd is ~25; (c) the benefit of capacity comes from pretraining it, not from RL alone (the 155/157 n-gram tables at width 384 lost 19-20 even though RL trained them too).
expected_delta: +6 central, -40..+40 theorems at >=7 on the 3-seed mean vs 153-claude's 687 (so 647-727). Mechanical: pretraining steps 4,300-4,700 per seed (loop unchanged; 153: 4540/4479/4489), handoff n_params exactly 9,963,792, held-out greedy 0.95-0.98 and final val loss 0.075-0.095 (153's band; the handed-off function is the trained 1280-unit model), RL sampling >= 200 samples/s. Mechanism check: round-1 targets solved inside 153's lottery (any 250-800), r1->r4 RL-solved gain larger than 153's seed-0 +391, r4 RL-solved mean above 153's 1172 (1157/1168/1191). Falsifier: r4 RL-solved mean below 1150 with metric below 687 rejects 'fresh units help RL learn'.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, pretrained exactly as 153-claude; at handoff every trunk MLP gains 88 fresh units (plasticity injection)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115/153): no rotation of q/k; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query pos - key pos) on the attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 on heads 1..4 and 0 on heads 5..8 (NoPE)
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 153-claude: pretraining (model, MTP, optimizers, schedule, batches, init) is byte-identical and trains d_ff 1280. After the loop, inject_fresh_units replaces each trunk block's fc1 Linear(384,1280) and fc2 Linear(1280,384) by Linear(384,1368) and Linear(1368,384): units 0..1279 copy the trained fc1 rows/biases and fc2 columns; the 88 fresh units get fc1 rows drawn N(0, std(trained fc1 weight of that block)) from the run's seeded GPU generator, fc1 bias 0, and fc2 columns exactly 0 (fc2 bias copied). The branch output is unchanged, so the handed-off function, held-out greedy, and the round-1 sampler are those of the trained 1280-unit model. RL's frozen AdamW then trains all 9,963,792 parameters, including the fresh ones. The MTP module is dropped as before (never widened)
arch.n_params_detail: handoff model: 9,963,792 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107; bench_pretrain on an A40 reported the same): per Peri-LN block 1,646,808 = qkv 443,520 + proj 147,840 + fc1 526,680 (1368x384 + 1368) + fc2 525,696 (384x1368 + 384) + 4 LayerNorms 3,072; emb + head 82,176; ln_f 768. Of these 406,032 = 6 x 88 x 769 are fresh at handoff. During pretraining the model has 153's 9,557,760 plus the dropped MTP module (1,875,584)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks whose fc1/fc2 are rebuilt as Linear(384, 1368)/Linear(1368, 384) (the state dict's shapes), then load state; the MTP module is not saved
arch.kv_cache: unchanged from 153 (the fork's preallocated per-block KV cache, key positions in caches[0]). CPU check with fork 51604b3 at full size (random orthogonal weights, perturbed biases/LN params): injection changes the full-forward logits by exactly 0.0; cached two-chunk decoding after injection matches the full forward to max abs diff 1.4e-6; loss_on backward gives nonzero gradients on the fresh fc2 columns (max 0.021) and exactly zero on the fresh fc1 rows until those columns move

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole. Muon never sees the 1368-unit matrices (they exist only after pretraining)
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights with the 88 fresh MLP units per trunk block added after the last pretraining step; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters() (the fresh units included)
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining (fc1/fc2 at 1280 units); the handoff model's parameters are 9,963,792

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); token-budget batches unchanged from 148/153
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged pretraining rule from 148/151/153: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)); LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0. Handoff-only: fresh fc1 rows N(0, std of the block's trained fc1 weight), fresh fc1 biases 0, fresh fc2 columns 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence): 618 steps in 60.4 s = 10.24 steps/s (153-claude's bench: 11.53; the pretraining loop is byte-identical to 153's, so this gap is pod-to-pod variance, not a cost), peak 7.4 GB (153: 7.42), n_params 9,963,792 after the handoff injection, sampling 246 samples/s on the injected model (153 bench 179; 153's RL rounds 225-256), bench sample_acc 0.035
